content.summary: Switch the live terminal on before the talk, present the deck, and switch it off after. The deck starts two sessions, a shell on slide 2 and Claude on slide 3, and comes back to both.

blocks.text: Turn the live terminal on from any shell. Nothing in the deck runs until it is on, and the status command says which way the switch is.

present terminal on
present terminal status
Both sessions start in the home directory. Point the Claude session at a repo by setting the same directory on both of its blocks, slides 3 and 7, before the talk.
Open the deck on localhost in Chrome when you plan to interrupt Claude with Escape. On a plain http host, Escape leaves fullscreen instead.
Claude shows its prompt a few seconds after the slide appears, longer when it first reports an MCP server that needs authentication. Give slide 3 that moment before pressing Enter.

items: Slide 2 starts the shell session with a ten minute tick loop typed on the prompt. Press Enter and move on.
Slide 3 starts Claude with a read-only question typed on the prompt. Press Enter and move on.
Slides 4 to 6 are talk slides. Both sessions keep running inside present serve.
Slide 7 shows the Claude session again with its answer, and slide 8 the shell with the ticks it printed meanwhile.
Run in a block's header starts a session that ended, and Kill ends one early.

blocks.text: Switching off ends every session the deck started within two seconds, and the list command shows that none is left.

present terminal off
present terminal list

sections.h: If a block does not start

items: The block says the live terminal is off: run the on command. The block starts by itself within a few seconds while its slide is showing.
The block names a missing directory: the directory on the block must exist on this machine.
The session ended: press Run in the block's header.
To end one session from the shell, give the kill command the page id and the session name.

deck.summary: A slide can start a shell or Claude, leave it running while you talk through the next slides, and show it again later with everything it did meanwhile.
deck.meta: 2026-10-19 · Demo · Live terminal block in present

sections.h: A shell starts on this slide and keeps running
sections.notes: Press Enter. The loop prints the time and a tick number once a second. Leave it running and move on; slide 8 comes back to it.

blocks.prefill: for i in {1..600}; do printf '%s  tick %03d\n' "$(date +%T)" "$i"; sleep 1; done

sections.h: Claude starts here and works while we move on
sections.notes: Give Claude a moment to show its prompt, then press Enter and move on within a few seconds. Slide 7 shows what it did.

blocks.prefill: explain in five lines what this directory holds and what you would read first

sections.h: The process belongs to the page, not to the tab
sections.notes: Both sessions are running inside present serve right now. Reload the tab or open the deck in a second window: the same two processes show.

blocks.text: Every slide that names the session shows the same process.

sections.h: A block that attaches again replays the recent output
sections.notes: The replay is what makes coming back to a slide work: the block shows what happened while it was off screen.

blocks.label: of output replayed on every reattach
blocks.sub: about 400 screens of an 80 by 30 terminal

sections.h: Nothing runs unless you switch it on
sections.notes: The switch lives in your shell, not on the page. The browser only ever sends keystrokes and the terminal size; what runs is read from the stored page.

items: Off by default, on only from your shell
Off ends every session within **two seconds**
The stored page says what runs, never the browser
A shared instance shows a placeholder and runs nothing

sections.notes: The same session as slide 3. Its answer is on screen and it takes input again.
